title: 03｜閱讀理解
description: 多篇商務文本題組，涵蓋主旨、細節、推論、字彙、NOT 題與跨文本整合。解析會指出線索在原文哪裡。

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Ms. Nadkarni's email?

options.text: To cancel a previously confirmed booking
options.rationale: 錯。信中從未提到取消，反而是在設法讓活動如期舉行（詢問是否有更大空間、討論替代方案）。

options.text: To raise concerns about a venue and request a solution
options.rationale: 對。整封信的骨架就是「提出兩個問題（投影機故障、報名人數超出容量）＋請對方提供解方」，句子 Could you advise whether a larger space is available 正是請求解決。

options.text: To request a refund for a faulty projector
options.rationale: 錯。她提到投影機故障，但要求的是「活動前修好」，全文沒有任何退款字眼。

options.text: To confirm the final catering numbers for an event
options.rationale: 錯。catering numbers 只出現在信末，用來說明「為何需要在 10/6 前回覆」，是時間理由而非寫信目的。

questions.explanation: (B) — 主旨題。整封信在反映場地兩個問題（投影機故障、人數超出）並請對方提供解方。(D) catering 只是附帶時間依據，非主旨。
questions.passageText:
Email

To: Marcus Bellamy m.bellamy@northgate-events.com From: Priya Nadkarni p.nadkarni@harlow-associates.com Date: October 2 Subject: Autumn Leadership Summit — Venue Concerns

Dear Mr. Bellamy,

I am writing regarding our booking for the Autumn Leadership Summit, scheduled to take place at the Northgate Conference Centre on November 8. As you know, Harlow Associates reserved the Grand Hall and two adjoining breakout rooms back in June, with an expected attendance of 240 delegates.

Two issues have come to my attention. First, when I visited the venue last week, I noticed that the Grand Hall's main projector was not functioning. Our opening keynote depends heavily on a video presentation, so this must be resolved well before the event. Second, our registrations have now climbed to 285 — considerably higher than our original estimate. I am concerned that the Grand Hall, which your website lists as accommodating 250 seated guests, may no longer be adequate.

Could you advise whether a larger space is available for that date? If not, we may need to discuss alternative seating arrangements or, as a last resort, cap our registration. I would appreciate a response by October 6, as we must confirm our catering numbers shortly thereafter.

Best regards, Priya Nadkarni Events Coordinator, Harlow Associates

Notice (posted at the Northgate Conference Centre, October 4)

NORTHGATE CONFERENCE CENTRE — Facility Update

Please be aware of the following changes affecting bookings in November:

The Grand Hall will undergo scheduled audiovisual upgrades from October 20 to October 31. All projection and sound equipment will be replaced with new units. Events booked from November 1 onward will benefit from the upgraded systems at no extra cost.
The Riverside Pavilion, our largest space (seated capacity 350), has recently become available for November following a cancellation. Clients wishing to transfer an existing booking to the Pavilion should contact their account manager. A transfer fee may apply.
The two breakout rooms adjoining the Grand Hall are unaffected and remain available as booked.

For questions, please contact the events office.

Internal Memo

To: Events Team From: Marcus Bellamy Date: October 5 Re: Harlow Associates booking

Team,

Following up on the Harlow Associates summit (Nov 8). I've reviewed their coordinator's concerns and here's how we'll proceed:

The projector issue resolves itself — the Grand Hall's entire AV system is being replaced later this month, so by their event date everything will be new. I'll reassure her on that point directly.

The capacity problem is the real one. At 285 registrations, the Grand Hall won't do. The Riverside Pavilion is now open for November and seats 350, which gives them ample room. I'm going to recommend they transfer. Given that the original shortfall wasn't their fault and they're a repeat client, I've decided we'll waive the transfer fee in this case. Please prepare the paperwork so I can offer this when I reply to her tomorrow.

One more thing: their breakout rooms stay exactly as they are — those aren't affected by any of this.

Thanks, Marcus

questions.prompt: According to the email, why is the malfunctioning projector a particular problem?

options.text: The venue charges extra for audiovisual equipment.
options.rationale: 錯。信中未提影音設備另外收費。

options.text: The breakout rooms have no projectors of their own.
options.rationale: 錯。breakout rooms 在信中只以「一併預訂」出現，沒有討論它們有無投影機。

options.text: The opening keynote relies on a video presentation.
options.rationale: 對。原句 Our opening keynote depends heavily on a video presentation 明確說明開場主題演講高度依賴影片，投影機因此格外關鍵。

options.text: The delegates were promised a live broadcast.
options.rationale: 錯。全文沒有提到向與會者承諾直播。

questions.explanation: (C) — 細節題。信中明言 Our opening keynote depends heavily on a video presentation，故投影機特別關鍵。

questions.prompt: By what date did Ms. Nadkarni request a reply?

options.rationale: 錯。10 月 2 日是這封信的寄件日期，不是要求回覆的期限。
錯。10 月 4 日是會議中心張貼公告的日期，與她的要求無關。
對。信末 I would appreciate a response by October 6 直接給出期限。
錯。11 月 8 日是活動舉行日。

questions.explanation: (C) October 6 — 細節題。信末 I would appreciate a response by October 6。陷阱：(D) Nov 8 是活動日、(A) Oct 2 是寄信日。

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the Grand Hall's seating capacity?

options.text: It is larger than the Riverside Pavilion's.
options.rationale: 錯。方向相反：Riverside Pavilion 可坐 350，Grand Hall 只有 250，Grand Hall 較小。

options.text: It is insufficient for the summit's current registration.
options.rationale: 對。網站列出 Grand Hall 可容納 250 人，而報名已達 285 人，兩個數字一比即知容量不足。這正是推論題的典型做法：把分散的兩個數據放在一起比較。

options.text: It was recently increased to 285 seats.
options.rationale: 錯。285 是報名人數，不是座位數；文中沒有提到座位增加。

options.text: It matches the number of breakout rooms.
options.rationale: 錯。breakout rooms 只有兩間，與 250 這個數字毫無關聯。

questions.explanation: (B) — 推論題。網站列 Grand Hall 可坐 250，但報名已達 285，故現有容量不足。陷阱：(A) 與 Pavilion（350）比較，Grand Hall 較小，敘述相反。

questions.prompt: According to the notice, what will happen to the Grand Hall in late October?

options.rationale: 錯。公告說的是升級工程，且明言 11 月起的活動可享用新設備，代表會繼續營運。

options.text: Its audiovisual equipment will be replaced.
options.rationale: 對。公告寫明 10/20 到 10/31 進行影音升級，All projection and sound equipment will be replaced with new units。

options.text: It will be merged with the Riverside Pavilion.
options.rationale: 錯。Riverside Pavilion 是另一個可供轉場的空間，公告沒有說要合併。

options.text: Its seating capacity will be reduced.
options.rationale: 錯。公告沒有提到座位數變動。

questions.explanation: (B) — 細節題。公告：10/20–10/31 進行影音升級、所有投影與音響設備汰換。

questions.prompt: Why does Mr. Bellamy consider the projector issue already solved?

options.text: A technician repaired it the previous week.
options.rationale: 錯。沒有任何技師維修的敘述；Nadkarni 上週看到時它仍是壞的。

options.text: The keynote will no longer use video.
options.rationale: 錯。改變演講形式是 Nadkarni 沒提、Bellamy 也沒提的方案。

options.text: The entire AV system is being replaced before the event.
options.rationale: 對。這題要串三份文件：Nadkarni 反映投影機壞了 → 公告說 10 月底全面汰換影音設備 → Bellamy 在備忘中寫 The projector issue resolves itself。原因就是設備會在活動前全數換新。

options.text: The event has been moved to a different room.
options.rationale: 錯。雖然 Bellamy 確實打算建議轉場，但他認定投影機問題已解決的理由是設備更新，不是換場地——換場地是為了解決人數問題。

questions.explanation: (C) — 整合題（信＋公告＋備忘）。Bellamy 認為投影機問題會自行解決，因整套 AV 系統本月稍晚全面更新，活動當天已是新設備。

questions.prompt: What does Mr. Bellamy decide to do for Harlow Associates?

options.rationale: 錯。備忘中完全沒有討論餐飲費用。

options.text: Waive the fee for transferring to a larger space
options.rationale: 對。備忘明寫 we'll waive the transfer fee in this case，理由是責任不在對方且屬長期客戶。

options.text: Provide an additional breakout room at no charge
options.rationale: 錯。備忘說 breakout rooms 維持原狀，沒有要免費加開。

options.text: Postpone the event until the following month
options.rationale: 錯。沒有任何延期的討論，反而是設法讓 11/8 如期舉行。

questions.explanation: (B) — 細節題。備忘：we'll waive the transfer fee（免除轉場費），讓對方轉到 Riverside Pavilion。

questions.prompt: What is indicated about the breakout rooms in both the notice and the memo?

options.text: They will be relocated to the second floor.
options.rationale: 錯。兩份文件都沒有提到搬到二樓。

options.text: They are being upgraded along with the Grand Hall.
options.rationale: 錯。公告特別把 breakout rooms 排除在影響範圍之外（unaffected）。

options.text: They remain unchanged from the original booking.
options.rationale: 對。公告說 remain available as booked，備忘說 stay exactly as they are，兩份文件的說法一致：維持原訂不變。這種「兩份文件都指出」的題型，答案必須在兩邊都找得到依據。

options.text: They are no longer available for November.
options.rationale: 錯。與兩份文件的敘述正好相反。

questions.explanation: (C) — 雙文本整合題。公告：breakout rooms unaffected and remain available as booked；備忘：their breakout rooms stay exactly as they are。兩者都說明維持原訂不變。

questions.prompt: The word "ample" in the memo is closest in meaning to

options.rationale: 錯。limited 是「有限的」，與句意相反——Pavilion 可坐 350 人而只需容納 285 人，空間是綽綽有餘。
錯。temporary 是「暫時的」，與空間大小無關。
對。ample room 指「充足的空間」，最接近 sufficient。判斷方法是回到句子：seats 350, which gives them ample room，350 大於 285，所以是「夠用、有餘裕」。
錯。expensive 談的是價格，句中談的是容納量。

questions.explanation: (C) sufficient — 字彙題。seats 350, which gives them ample room＝充足的空間，ample≈sufficient。

questions.prompt: Which concern raised by Ms. Nadkarni does Mr. Bellamy NOT directly address in his memo?

options.rationale: 錯。Bellamy 在備忘第一點就處理了投影機問題（設備將全面更新）。
錯。他把人數問題視為 the real one，並提出轉到 Riverside Pavilion 的方案。

options.text: The status of the breakout rooms
options.rationale: 錯。備忘最後一段明確交代 breakout rooms 維持原狀。
對。catering numbers 只是 Nadkarni 用來解釋回覆期限的理由，Bellamy 的備忘從頭到尾沒有回應這一點。NOT 題的解法是逐一為其他三個選項在文中找到對應句，找不到的那個就是答案。

questions.explanation:
(D) — NOT / 整合題。Nadkarni 提出：投影機（Bellamy 有回應）、超額人數（有回應）、breakout rooms 狀態（有回應）。catering numbers 只是她自己的時程理由，Bellamy 備忘中未直接處理 → 答案 D。

評分與能力估算框架

請填入實際作答結果後，我會依此產出與 A、B 相同格式的完整分析。

需回報的資料：

questions.focusPoint: 細節題（門檻數字的套用）
questions.passageText:
Internal Memorandum

To: Regional Operations Managers
From: Olivia Cheng, Director of Corporate Operations
Date: August 18
Subject: Revised Equipment Replacement and Maintenance Program

As part of our ongoing effort to reduce operating costs while maintaining service quality, the Executive Committee has approved a revised equipment replacement and maintenance program that will take effect on September 15. Although many aspects of the current policy remain unchanged, several important procedures have been modified.

Under the previous policy, regional offices could independently authorize the replacement of office equipment with an original purchase price of up to US$4,000. Beginning September 15, however, only equipment with an original purchase price below US$2,500 may be replaced without approval from Corporate Procurement. Requests involving equipment valued at US$2,500 or more must include a cost-benefit analysis comparing repair costs with replacement costs. Managers should note that purchase price -- not current market value -- will be used when determining approval requirements.

Routine preventive maintenance schedules will also be adjusted. Previously, offices were expected to perform inspections every six months regardless of equipment usage. Under the revised program, devices that are used fewer than 20 hours per week may be inspected annually, while equipment exceeding 20 hours of weekly use must continue following the existing six-month schedule.

To improve inventory accuracy, all replaced equipment must remain at the regional office until collection has been confirmed by the contracted recycling vendor. Several offices have recently experienced delays because discarded equipment was transferred to temporary storage facilities before pickup appointments were scheduled. Beginning in September, any office that transfers equipment before vendor confirmation may be held responsible for additional transportation charges.

Managers planning large-scale office renovations should also be aware that replacement requests submitted as part of renovation projects will be reviewed separately from routine replacement requests. Although renovation-related purchases may qualify for additional funding, approval processing typically requires approximately two weeks longer than standard requests because both the Facilities Department and Corporate Procurement must review the documentation.

Finally, managers are reminded that employees should not delay reporting equipment malfunctions simply because replacement approval is pending. Safety-related repairs must always be completed immediately, even if the equipment is expected to be replaced within the following months. The company believes that preventing workplace accidents should always take priority over short-term budget considerations.

Questions regarding these procedures should be submitted through the Corporate Operations Portal rather than by email. This change is intended to ensure that inquiries are tracked consistently and answered in the order received.
questions.prompt: A regional office wants to replace a printer that originally cost US$3,200. According to the memorandum, what must the office do before replacement can be approved?

options.text: Wait until the next annual maintenance inspection.
options.rationale: 錯。年度檢查屬於第三段的「預防性保養」規定，與第二段的汰換核准流程是兩條不同的線，文中沒有把兩者綁在一起。

options.text: Obtain confirmation from the recycling vendor.
options.rationale: 錯。回收商確認出現在第四段，管的是「舊設備何時可以搬離辦公室」，是汰換之後的事，不是核准的前置條件。

options.text: Submit documentation comparing repair and replacement costs.
options.rationale: 對。3,200 美元 ≥ 2,500 美元的門檻，第二段明訂 Requests involving equipment valued at US$2,500 or more must include a cost-benefit analysis comparing repair costs with replacement costs。

options.text: Demonstrate that the printer's current market value exceeds US$2,500.
options.rationale: 錯。這是為粗心讀者設的陷阱。第二段最後一句特別澄清 purchase price -- not current market value -- will be used，判斷依據是原始購價而非現值。

questions.explanation: 這類題要做兩步：先把題目給的數字（3,200）對到文中的門檻（2,500），確認落在哪一區間；再回原文抓該區間對應的具體要求。文中特意加了一句「用購價不用現值」，就是為了製造選項 D 這個陷阱。

questions.focusPoint: 細節題（因果條件的辨識）
questions.prompt: Which situation would most likely result in additional transportation charges?

options.text: Equipment is inspected every six months although it is rarely used.
options.rationale: 錯。使用率低的設備依新制「可以」改為年檢，但仍照半年檢查並不違規，文中也沒有為此設任何罰則。

options.text: Equipment is moved to temporary storage before pickup has been confirmed.
options.rationale: 對。第四段先說明問題成因（設備在約定取件前就被移到臨時倉庫），再直接寫出後果：any office that transfers equipment before vendor confirmation may be held responsible for additional transportation charges。

options.text: A renovation request requires review by two departments.
options.rationale: 錯。第五段說兩個部門會審，造成的後果是「多花約兩週」的時間成本，不是運輸費用。

options.text: Safety repairs are completed before replacement approval is granted.
options.rationale: 錯。最後一段的立場正好相反：安全相關維修必須立即執行，這是被鼓勵的行為，不會受罰。

questions.explanation: 備忘錄型文章常把「問題 → 新規定 → 罰則」寫在同一段。找罰則題時直接搜尋 charges、responsible for、subject to 這類字眼，通常一句就命中。其他選項的干擾方式是把文中「別段的後果」搬過來張冠李戴。

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of the memorandum?

options.text: To announce several procedural changes affecting equipment management.
options.rationale: 對。開頭就說 the Executive Committee has approved a revised... program，接著逐段說明核准門檻、保養週期、舊機處置、翻新案審查等四項變動，是典型的「多項程序異動公告」。

options.text: To explain why equipment maintenance should be outsourced.
options.rationale: 錯。文中唯一的外部廠商是回收商，且只負責收取舊機；保養仍由各區辦公室自行執行，全文沒有主張外包。

options.text: To encourage managers to increase spending on office renovations.
options.rationale: 錯。翻新只在第五段出現，講的是審查流程更久、需兩個部門會簽，語氣是提醒而非鼓勵；全文主軸也是降低營運成本。

options.text: To summarize the financial performance of regional offices.
options.rationale: 錯。文中沒有任何營運績效數字，出現的金額都是核准門檻。

questions.explanation: 主旨題的可靠做法是看「涵蓋範圍」：正解必須罩得住全文每一段。B、C、D 各自只對應到一段甚至半段，屬於以偏概全；A 的 several procedural changes 正好對應四個段落各講一項異動。
